reader.requirement: At 1985, for any depth of nesting, a SIGN clause written on a subordinate group overrides an enclosing group's SIGN clause for every signed DISPLAY numeric item of that subordinate group (LEADING/TRAILING, with or without SEPARATE), which fixes those items' storage image and size.

edition-consulted.switches: below 2002 (DialectLevel < 2002) refuses a group SIGN clause with no signed subordinate or one reaching a non-DISPLAY signed item (constructs SignGroupUnsignedSubordinates2002 / SignGroupNondisplaySubordinate2002); it walks only the subordinates the group's clause reaches, honouring a nearer clause (GR2/GR3)

reader.edition-search: grep Edition|Dialect|Version in InheritSignClausesPass.cs and DataBinder.cs#InheritSignWalk/WithInheritedSign: none; the precedence walk (item.OwnSign ?? inherited) is edition-blind. CheckSignClausesPass#GateGroupSignSubordinates is the only edition switch near the rule.
reader.behaviour-differs-by-edition: no: precedence is the same code at 85 and 2023; only the 1985 SR1/SR2 group-subject refusals differ (2002 relaxations)
reader.witnesses-cover: part: g85_bf11_06 covers one subordinate group level with SEPARATE on every clause, Working-Storage only; not an embedded (non-SEPARATE) override, a three-level nest, or a file record

probes.expected: G LEADING SEPARATE > SUB TRAILING (embedded) > SUB2 LEADING SEPARATE: S1 takes SUB's embedded trailing (-12 -> 01K), S5 takes SUB2's (-012), S6/S2/S4 their own clauses (034+, -012, 00G), S3 G's (-012); values preserved through MOVE/ADD
FD record FR TRAILING SEPARATE > FS LEADING SEPARATE: FA '-01', FB own TRAILING embedded '0K', FC FR's '03-'; read back equal

probes.printed: COBOL2422 for C (COMP with own SIGN); COBOL0900 for HS over HC (USAGE BINARY) requires COBOL-2002; no diagnostic charged to H for HC
probes.expected: 1985 SR2: the entries a SIGN clause applies to must be DISPLAY; the clause that applies to HC is HS's (GR2), so HS is refused and H is not

citations.check: OK  §1985:VI.5.12.4 GR2  (5.12.4 General Rules)  the text is in GR2

reader.notes: InheritSignWalk hands each item the nearest enclosing written clause (item.OwnSign ?? inherited) and applies it only to signed DISPLAY numerics, so a subordinate group's clause wins for its subtree. Probes over embedded/separate mixes, three levels and an FD record print the expected images.

refuter.evidence: Probe sg1.cob (sg1-002) put a group with SIGN TRAILING SEPARATE over a subgroup with SIGN LEADING (embedded) under OCCURS 2. The subgroup was redefined by a group with SIGN LEADING SEPARATE, and a 66 alias renamed an item of the outer group. It printed G1=[12-L45OG80R07]: each table occurrence takes the subgroup's embedded leading sign (L4, G8), and the REDEFINES subgroup's own clause wins over the outer one (G3=[11--04+210R07]). Probes sg2 and sg3 used an FD with CODE-SET (STANDARD-1) whose record has SIGN LEADING (embedded). sg2, where the subgroup's TRAILING SEPARATE takes precedence for FA, compiled and wrote FR=[05-+06]. sg3 added an item that only the record's embedded clause reaches and was refused with COBOL1672 (§1985:VI.5.12.3 SR3). So precedence decides which entries SR3 reaches. cite.py: OK §1985:VI.5.12.4 GR2; OK §1985:VI.5.12.3 SR3.
